text.p: The United Arab Emirates (UAE), a tax-free haven and one of the Gulf states most eager to lure foreign capital, has no plans to levy corporate or individual taxes, a senior government official said.

"It is not expected that any taxes would be imposed as this would mean radical changes to the financial policy," Sheikh Fahem bin Mohammad al-Qassimi, Minister of Commerce and Economy, said in remarks which will be published in Saturday's issue of Emirates Today but made available to Reuters on Friday.
"Taxes can have a negative impact on the national economic performance and investment and should accordingly be avoided," he said.

Sheikh Fahem put 1996 private sector investments in the Gulf state at 41 billion dirhams ($11.2 billion) and said the UAE intends to continue supporting what he described as "an investment-friendly" atmosphere.

The UAE, member of the six-state Gulf Cooperation Council --which also includes Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, Qatar, Bahrain and Oman-- is seeking to diversify its oil-dominated economy by relaxing rules on foreign investments, luring private capital and actively implementing an industrial development plan.
